liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Oh Babe It Ain't No Lie** (1 other source): Notes say the previous Ain't No Lie was on 12-6-80 [1]
- **Ripple** (1 other source): Notes mark this as the final acoustic Ripple, with the last electric one on 9-3-88 [1]
- **Hully Gully** (1 review): Reviewer says this is the only performance of Hully Gully [13]
- **Gloria** (1 review): Reviewer says Gloria and Lovelight had been absent from setlists for a very long time [13]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (1 review): Reviewer says it was the first Lovelight in nearly ten years [16]

## The recordings

- **gd1981-10-16.mtx.chappell.sb27.95431.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 116 min; rated 4.5/5 by 6 [1]
- **gd1981-10-16.mtx.seamons.110497.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 116 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd81-10-16.sbd.vinson.1217.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 118 min; rated 3.88/5 by 24 [3]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the mix fluctuates in level; Reviewer finds the recording quality only so-so [17][21]
- **gd1981-10-16.147841.mtx.tobin.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 18 songs; 110 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [9]

## Around the show

- Played on Bob Weir's 34th birthday, with the band sounding relaxed and happy [13]
- Bobby is audibly in high spirits at the start of the recording [17]
- Reviewer describes a loose, relaxed show that led to a varied second set [22]
- Club show with borrowed instruments, an acoustic set and Bob's birthday [23]
- Set 1 was acoustic [2]
- Set I was Bobby and Jerry playing acoustic on borrowed instruments [9]
- Reviewer rates it above most 1981 shows, with both acoustic and electric sets strong [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1981-10-16.mtx.chappell.sb27.95431.flac16**: transferred by Chris Chappell; source: Matrix mix (SBD/AUD) [1]. Also: Matrix blends an audience source from Michel the Belgian Deadhead; the uploader held it two years awaiting video sync [1]
- **gd1981-10-16.mtx.seamons.110497.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix by Hunter Seamons using Final Cut Pro (SHN & FLAC > AIFF > Final Cut w/EQ > AIFF CD tracking via Audacity > FLAC16 via xACT) [2]. Also: Source is Cindy Poris's opened soundboard, taken to Sony/TDK cassette master, then a Nakamichi DR-1 cassette master; Charlie Miller transferred via Sound Devices 744T at 24-bit/96k, mastered in Audition and Samplitude, then FLAC16 [2]
- **gd81-10-16.sbd.vinson.1217.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [3]. Also: A soundboard source is welcome, since a widely circulated audience recording had been the version available before [14]
- **gd1981-10-16.147841.mtx.tobin.flac16**: transferred by SBD + AUD Matrix 2 Source Mix (44/16) by Kevin Tobin; source: SBD + AUD Matrix 2 Source Mix (44/16) [9]. Also: Mixed by an archive.org user; Trader Little Helper converted it to FLAC on 28 October 2019 [9]
